title: Impact of Pasir Gudang Incident in Johor on Singaporeans
what_it_is: Impact of Pasir Gudang Incident in Johor on Singaporeans

sections.label: Punggol VOC sensors and Pasir Gudang
sections.summary: Asked what sensors measure volatile organic compounds in Punggol air and whether levels rose since the Pasir Gudang dumping.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what specific sensors are there in place in Punggol to measure the level of volatile organic compounds in the air; and (b) whether there has been an increase in the measured levels since the chemical waste dumping incident in Pasir Gudang.

sections.label: Johoreans ill from Sungai Kim Kim dumping
sections.summary: Media reports say over 3,000 Johoreans fell ill after 20 to 40 tonnes of chemical waste were dumped into Sungai Kim Kim.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: According to media reports, since 7 March 2019, more than 3,000 Johoreans fell ill as a result of the illegal dumping of around 20 to 40 tonnes of chemical waste into Sungai Kim Kim, a river in Pasir Gudang.

sections.label: Soil and polluted water removed
sections.summary: More than 900 tonnes of soil and 1,500 tonnes of polluted water have been removed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: More than 900 tonnes of soil and 1,500 tonnes of polluted water have been removed.

sections.label: PUB oil booms on Singapore coast
sections.summary: As a precaution, PUB installed oil booms at outlet drains and estuaries along Singapore's north and north-eastern coast.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As a precautionary measure, PUB has installed oil booms at the outlet drains and estuaries along the north and north-eastern coast of Singapore.

sections.label: SFA seafood tests find no anomalies
sections.summary: SFA tests of seafood from these fish farms for PAHs, VOCs and heavy metals detected no anomalies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Singapore Food Agency's (SFA's) tests of seafood samples from these fish farms for compounds, such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), VOCs and heavy metals, have not detected any anomalies.

sections.label: Smells and ambient air readings
sections.summary: By morning the sun and stronger wind dilute and disperse odours, and smells show no direct correlation with ambient air quality readings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, by daytime, in the morning, the sun is up and the wind speed has gathered strength, it then gets diluted and dispersed away.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But let me say that there is no direct correlation or association between the smells – burning smell or chemical smell – and the ambient air quality readings.

sections.label: Flaring process gases safety
sections.summary: Flaring safely burns process gases into carbon dioxide and water vapour, so there would be no health impact from the flaring.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Actually, flaring will safely burn these process gases off into carbon dioxide and water vapour so that there would not be any health impact due to this flaring.
